questions.q: Why does the "Close All Tasks" UI Action use GlideModal rather than GlideDialogWindow for its confirmation?
options: The confirmation is just a message, a task count, and a date — not a custom form needing its own UI Page
GlideDialogWindow cannot be called from a UI Action's client script
GlideModal is required whenever a UI Action closes records
GlideModal runs on the server while GlideDialogWindow does not
questions.explain: GlideModal is the right fit for a simple message/confirmation; a custom UI Page via GlideDialogWindow would be unnecessary here.

options: It re-submits the form with an action name so the UI Action's server-side script runs only after the user confirms
It immediately deletes the current record without any server call
It cancels the GlideModal without running any further script
It opens a second GlideDialogWindow on top of the first
questions.explain: gsftSubmit triggers the form submission the server script checks for, ensuring the server-side close logic only runs after a confirmed click.

questions.q: Why is formatShortDate() placed in a UI Script named DateFormatHelpers rather than written inline in the UI Action's client script?
options: Because a separate, unrelated Client Script on the same form also needs the identical formatting logic, and a shared UI Script avoids duplicating it
Because UI Actions are not allowed to contain any inline JavaScript functions
Because GlideModal requires all helper functions to live in a UI Script by platform rule
Because Script Includes cannot be called from client-side code
questions.explain: The same function is needed by two different callers on the form — the textbook case for extracting it into a shared UI Script.

options: Every open (active) task record whose parent is the current Change Request
Every task record in the entire instance, regardless of parent
Only the current Change Request record itself
Every closed task related to any change request
questions.explain: The two addQuery calls filter to task records whose parent matches the current record and whose active flag is true.

questions.q: What happens if the user clicks Cancel in the GlideModal confirmation?
options: The onPromptComplete callback receives confirmed as false, gsftSubmit is never called, and the server-side close script never runs
The server-side script runs anyway regardless of the user's choice
The form is deleted immediately
A second confirmation dialog opens automatically
questions.explain: The `if (confirmed)` check guards the gsftSubmit call — without a true confirmation, the server-side task-closing logic never executes.
